healthy.description: No visible disease symptoms detected. The leaf appears healthy.
healthy.symptoms: Uniform green color, no spots, pustules or powdery growth.
healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Continue standard crop management and monitoring.

leaf_rust.description: Fungal disease caused by Puccinia triticina. One of the most common and damaging wheat diseases worldwide.
leaf_rust.symptoms: Small, round, orange-brown pustules (uredinia) scattered mainly on the upper leaf surface.
leaf_rust.treatment: Apply triazole or strobilurin fungicides at early infection. Use resistant wheat varieties. Remove crop residues and avoid late nitrogen fertilization.

stripe_rust.description: Fungal disease caused by Puccinia striiformis. Spreads rapidly in cool, humid conditions and can cause severe yield losses.
stripe_rust.symptoms: Yellow-orange powdery pustules arranged in long stripes along the leaf veins.
stripe_rust.treatment: Apply fungicides (e.g., tebuconazole, propiconazole) at first sign of disease. Plant resistant cultivars and avoid early sowing in humid regions.

powdery_mildew.description: Fungal disease caused by Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici. Common in dense, heavily fertilized crops.
powdery_mildew.symptoms: White to gray powdery fungal patches on leaf surfaces, which may later turn brown and cover whole leaves.
powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply sulfur-based or triazole fungicides. Improve field ventilation, avoid excessive nitrogen, and use resistant varieties.

septoria.description: Fungal disease caused by Zymoseptoria tritici (formerly Septoria tritici). Favored by wet, moderate-temperature weather.
septoria.symptoms: Irregular, elongated tan-brown lesions with small black fruiting bodies (pycnidia) inside the lesions.
septoria.treatment: Apply fungicides at flag-leaf stage. Rotate crops, plow under residues, and choose tolerant varieties.
